description: The World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates (WASDE) is a monthly USDA report giving annual forecasts of supply and use for United States and world wheat, rice, coarse grains, oilseeds and cotton, and United States supply and use of sugar, meat, poultry, eggs and milk, as well as Mexico's sugar. It is prepared by the World Agricultural Outlook Board, which chairs Interagency Commodity Estimates Committees of analysts from USDA agencies who interpret USDA and other domestic and foreign information. Coverage is the United States and the world by major producers and importers, with an archive from 1973 to the present. Each report, released at noon Eastern time on scheduled dates such as 11 September 2026, is available free in PDF, XML, Excel and text, with consolidated historical data from 2010 to 2025 in CSV updated the day after each release and a visualisation. Caveats: values are forecasts revised month by month, and the definitions of marketing years differ across commodities and countries. For simulation it gives balance sheets of production, trade, use and stocks to calibrate food supply chain models and to test how droughts or export restrictions change global grain availability. It is related to the USDA PSD Online record in this catalogue, which holds the underlying country series.
